task_instance: Scaffold a fresh Expo (SDK 57) app, add a DOM component (components/WebChart.tsx with the 'use dom' directive) that renders a web-only library (recharts LineChart) not usable in plain React Native, wire it into App.tsx as a normal-looking component, and verify it actually works for both the 'web' target (renders as-is) and the 'ios' target (bundled into an isolated WebView bundle), per the skill's core promise.
tools_used: shell (npx create-expo-app, npm install, npx expo export)
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/expo__skills__expo-dom/myapp . Steps: `npx create-expo-app@latest myapp --template blank-typescript` scaffolded Expo SDK 57 app. `npx expo install ...` failed with 'HTTP Proxy Network Error: Forbidden' on its React Native Directory compatibility check, so fell back to `npm install react-dom react-native-web react-native-webview recharts @expo/metro-runtime`, which succeeded via the plain npm registry. Created components/WebChart.tsx starting with `'use dom';` that imports and renders recharts' LineChart/XAxis/YAxis/CartesianGrid/Tooltip (a browser-only charting library incompatible with bare React Native), typed with `dom?: import('expo/dom').DOMProps`. Wired it into App.tsx exactly like a normal component: `<WebChart data={[...]} dom={{ style: { width: 400, height: 340 } }} />`. Verified the deliverable two ways: (1) `npx expo export -p web` succeeded ('Web Bundled ... 757 modules', produced dist/_expo/static/js/web/*.js) and `grep -l recharts` on the output bundle confirmed the chart code is present, i.e. it 'renders as-is on web'. (2) `npx expo export -p ios` succeeded after installing @expo/metro-runtime, printing both 'iOS Bundled ... index.ts' and a separate 'DOM Bundled ... components/WebChart.tsx (710 modules)' step, producing dist/www.bundle/<hash>.html and dist/www.bundle/<hash>.js -- the isolated WebView bundle Expo injects into WKWebView on iOS. Inspected that generated www.bundle/*.html: it contains the expected 'Root element for the DOM component', a `<div id="root">`, `window.ReactNativeWebView.injectedObjectJson()` prop-injection bootstrap, and loads the js bundle. `grep -o recharts www.bundle/*.js` and `grep -o 'Chart Data' www.bundle/*.js` both matched, confirming the web-only recharts library and component content were correctly bundled into the isolated DOM/WebView context exactly as the skill describes ('DOM components run in isolated context', 'runs web code verbatim in a webview on native'). No actual iOS/Android simulator was available or needed to verify this core mechanism, since Expo's bundler produces the concrete webview payload as a build artifact that can be inspected directly.
